CYP3A4 Substrates and Serious Events: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF should not be co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates that are associated with serious or life-threatening events due to elevated plasma concentrations. 2. Zuranolone Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases zuranolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and the zuranolone dose reduced when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Close monitoring is required. 3. Acetazolamide Interaction: Acetazolamide may increase the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, but monitoring is advised. 4. Anastrozole Interaction: Anastrozole may increase the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 5. Cyclophosphamide Interaction: Cyclophosphamide may increase the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF through CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, and monitoring is advised. 6. Proton Pump Inhibitors (PPIs): Based on studies with the components of Stribild, no clinically significant interactions are expected when co-administered with PPIs such as esomeprazole, lansoprazole, omeprazole, pantoprazole, or rabeprazole. 7. Drospirenone Interaction: Drospirenone may increase the levels of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, but monitoring is recommended. 8. Ganaxolone Interaction: 9. Ixazomib Interaction: 10. Abacavir Contraindication: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is a complete HIV regimen and should not be co-administered with other antiretrovirals, including abacavir. 11. Abemaciclib Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases abemaciclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of abemaciclib is required, and close monitoring is necessary. 12. Acalabrutinib Interaction: Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A inhibitor is necessary, acalabrutinib treatment should be temporarily interrupted. 13. Acyclovir Interaction: Co-administration of acyclovir with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Adagrasib Interaction: Avoid co-administration of adagrasib, a CYP3A4 substrate, with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors until steady-state concentrations are achieved. Monitoring is required to avoid toxicity. 15. Adefovir Interaction: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Ado-Trastuzumab Emtansine Interaction: Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Alfentanil Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases alfentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 18. Alfuzosin Contraindication: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is contraindicated due to the risk of serious or life-threatening events from elevated plasma concentrations. 19. Alprazolam Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases alprazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose reduction of benzodiazepines should be considered, and close monitoring is required. 20. Aluminum Hydroxide Interaction: Aluminum hydroxide decreases elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours is recommended. 21. Ambrisentan Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases ambrisentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 22. Amikacin Interaction: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Amiodarone Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases amiodarone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 24. Amitriptyline Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases amitriptyline levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution is advised with CYP2D6 substrates, and close monitoring is required. 25. Amlodipine Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases amlodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 26. Amoxapine Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases amoxapine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Caution is advised with CYP2D6 substrates, and close monitoring is required. 27. Amphotericin B Interaction: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Apalutamide Interaction: Co-administration with apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels. Avoid co-administration or substitute another drug. 29. Aprepitant Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases aprepitant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 30. Aripiprazole Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases aripiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 31. Armodafinil Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases armodafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 32. Aspirin Interaction: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase nephrotoxicity. Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered, and close monitoring is required. 33. Atazanavir Contraindication: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is contraindicated due to potential interactions. 34. Atogepant Interaction: When co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, the recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg once daily. Close monitoring is required. 35. Atomoxetine Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases atomoxetine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 36. Atorvastatin Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases atorvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Initiate atorvastatin at the lowest dose and titrate carefully, not exceeding 20 mg/day. 37. Axitinib Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases axitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 38. Bacitracin Interaction: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Bedaquiline Interaction: Avoid co-administration of bedaquiline with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than 14 consecutive days unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 40. Belzutifan Interaction: Belzutifan may decrease elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF levels. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 41. Benzhydrocodone Interaction: Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Close monitoring is required. 42. Benzphetamine Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases benzphetamine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 43. Betaxolol Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases betaxolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 44. Betibeglogene Autotemcel Interaction: Antiretroviral medications should not be taken for at least one month before mobilization or apheresis cycles, as they may interfere with cell manufacturing. 45. Bortezomib Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases bortezomib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 46. Bosentan Interaction: Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is contraindicated due to potential interactions. 47. Brexpiprazole Interaction: Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also using a CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the dose. 48. Brigatinib Interaction: If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the brigatinib dose by 50%. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 49. Bromocriptine Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases bromocriptine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 50. Budesonide Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases budesonide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 51. Buprenorphine Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases buprenorphine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 52. Bupropion Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases bupropion levels by an unknown mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Buspirone Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases buspirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 54. Busulfan Interaction: Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases busulfan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 55. Cabozantinib Interaction: Avoid co-administration of cabozantinib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If required, reduce the cabozantinib dose and resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 56. Calcifediol Interaction: CYP450 inhibitors may alter vitamin D metabolism, potentially affecting calcifediol serum levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
